title: Quotient of a connected Galois cover by a subgroup
statement: Let $U$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme], let $G$ be a finite group, and let $c:E\to U$ be a finite etale morphism with $E$ connected which is a Galois cover with group $G$ [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]: $G$ acts on $E$ over $U$, $E/G\cong U$, and $G$ acts simply transitively on every geometric fibre of $c$. Let $H\le G$ be a subgroup, acting on $E$ by restriction. Let $\pi:E\to Z$ be a morphism of $U$-schemes which is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], satisfies $\mathcal O_Z=(\pi_*\mathcal O_E)^H$, and is a categorical quotient of $E$ by $H$ in schemes: every $H$-invariant morphism from $E$ to a scheme factors uniquely through $\pi$. Then $\pi$ is surjective, the structure morphism $v:Z\to U$ is finite etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], $Z$ is connected, and every geometric fibre of $v$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre] has exactly $[G:H]$ points. The cases $H=1$ and $H=G$ are included.

source.place: Lemma 03BK (groupoids-lemma-invariants-base-change), part (3): formation of invariants of a finite group commutes with flat base change, applied after an etale base change trivializing the torsor (E becomes G x U', its H-quotient (G/H) x U'). Used in ILO XVI 3.7, p.255, for the generic degree [G:H] of X''/H over X.

proof.text: The Galois-cover hypothesis says that $c$ is a $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. In particular $c$ is surjective and the map $\alpha:\coprod_{g\in G}E\to E\times_UE$, $(g,e)\mapsto(ge,e)$, is an isomorphism. To verify this also from the stated geometric-fibre criterion, view $\alpha$ over the second factor $E$. Its source and target are finite etale over $E$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]; the disjoint copies of $E$ are the scheme coproduct of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and the fold is finite etale since on an affine open it is the finite product of identity algebras. Since $E$ is nonempty and connected, choose a geometric point of $E$. The functor in [lem-fet-galois-category] reflects isomorphisms by [def-galois-category]. Its value on $\alpha$ is the bijection $g\mapsto ge$ from $G$ to the $c$-fibre over the chosen geometric point of $E$, by simple transitivity. Thus $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. Every geometric fibre of $c$ is nonempty by the torsor hypothesis, giving surjectivity on underlying points as well.

source.place: Section 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois); torsor identity, checked by the conservative geometric fibre functor

proof.text: Restrict the action to $H$. The map $\coprod_{h\in H}E\to E\times_UE$ is the inclusion of the $H$-summands of $\coprod_{g\in G}E$ followed by $\alpha$, so it is a monomorphism. Finite morphisms are affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; hence $E\to U$ is affine. Apply [lem-per-free-finite-group-affine-quotient] with base $U$, total scheme $E$ and group $H$. It gives a quotient $q:E\to Q$ with structure map $w:Q\to U$. The map $q$ is surjective, represents the fppf orbit sheaf, is categorical over $U$, and remains the orbit-sheaf quotient after every base change on $U$.

source.place: Tag 07S7 (lemma-quotient-scheme), affine case applied to the restricted action

proof.text: Use the two categorical properties with their maps fixed. The given $\pi$ is $H$-invariant, so $\pi=a\circ q$ for a unique $U$-map $a:Q\to Z$. Conversely $q$ is invariant, so $q=b\circ\pi$ for a unique scheme map $b:Z\to Q$. The equality $w\circ b\circ\pi=c=v\circ\pi$ implies $w\circ b=v$ by uniqueness of factorization through $\pi$, so $b$ is a $U$-map. Now $(a\circ b)\circ\pi=\pi$ and $(b\circ a)\circ q=q$; uniqueness for the two quotients gives $a\circ b=1_Z$ and $b\circ a=1_Q$. Thus $a$ identifies the actual given quotient with $q$, respecting the quotient maps and the structure maps. In particular $\pi$ is surjective since $q$ is.

source.place: Tag 07S7 (lemma-quotient-scheme), uniqueness of the categorical quotient; explicit two-sided inverse argument

proof.text: Pull back along $c:E\to U$. The isomorphism $\alpha$ identifies $E\times_UE$ over its second factor with $\coprod_{g\in G}E$. Under this identification $h\in H$ sends $(g,e)$ to $(hg,e)$. By the base-change assertion of [lem-per-free-finite-group-affine-quotient], $Z\times_UE$ is its orbit-sheaf quotient. That quotient is $\coprod_{Hg\in H\backslash G}E$, with the leg sending the $g$-copy identically to the $Hg$-copy: on any test scheme a map to these coproducts is a locally constant choice of label and a map to $E$; a coset label lifts locally to a $G$-label, and two lifts differ locally by an $H$-label. This gives mutually inverse maps on the sheafified orbit presheaf. Consequently the projection $Z\times_UE\to E$ is the fold map of $[G:H]$ copies. It is finite etale: over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset E$ its coordinate algebra is $\prod_{H\backslash G}A$, finite free, flat and etale (each factor is the identity algebra).

source.place: Tag 07S7 (lemma-quotient-scheme): base change of the represented orbit sheaf; explicit calculation of the quotient of the trivial torsor

proof.text: The singleton $\{c:E\to U\}$ is an fpqc covering in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Indeed $c$ is flat because it is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and it is surjective by Step 1; for each affine open $V\subset U$, its inverse image is a single affine open since $c$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and its image is $V$. The base change of $v$ along this covering is finite etale by Step 4. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] and [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] to conclude that $v$ is finite and etale. No Noetherian or separation hypothesis on $U$ is required.

Fix any geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$. Simple transitivity gives a lift $e:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to E$. Pull Step 4 back along $e$ and use the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]: since $c\circ e=s$, this gives $Z\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\simeq\coprod_{H\backslash G}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Therefore its geometric fibre in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre] has $|H\backslash G|=[G:H]$ points. Here $H\backslash G$ is the set of right cosets; inversion gives a bijection $Hg\mapsto g^{-1}H$ with the left cosets defining the index, so no normality assumption is used. The scheme $Z$ is nonempty because $E$ is nonempty and $\pi$ is surjective. If $Z$ were the disjoint union of two nonempty open-and-closed subsets, their inverse images under $\pi$ would be two nonempty open-and-closed subsets partitioning $E$, contradicting [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Thus $Z$ is connected. For $H=1$ the coset set has $|G|$ elements, and for $H=G$ it has one; all preceding constructions include both cases.

The new node matches the affine case of 07S7 hypothesis by hypothesis: K_S is finite locally free, freeness means j is a monomorphism, and X->S is affine. Its torsor, finite-locally-free-and-surjective, base-change and categorical clauses each follow in a few lines from the fppf torsor conclusion and the fact that schemes are fppf sheaves. I tested it on K=1, X empty, the swap on S⊔S, translation with char dividing |K|, and the trivial non-free action, which is correctly excluded. It is not a duplicate: lem-a1-finite-flat-affine-relation-quotient needs global affineness, lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient has a Noetherian base and no torsor conclusion, lem-weil-pbc-connected-torsor-subgroup-quotient is only existential, and Mathlib has nothing (ColimitsOver is gluing). Step 1 derives alpha as an isomorphism from simple transitivity on fibres, using the reflection clause of the Galois category FEt(E). Step 2 checks that the restricted action is monomorphic and E->U affine. Step 3 gives explicit inverse U-isomorphisms compatible with pi and q, so the given pi is pinned. Step 4 identifies the base change as the coset-labelled coproduct; I checked the sheaf calculation. Step 5 checks the singleton fpqc covering and cites the exact finite and étale descent nodes. Step 6 counts [G:H] points per geometric fibre, also for non-normal H, and proves connectedness. The item statement is unchanged, stmt_deps and proof_deps are consistent and no SGA is cited. I accept the three declared generic tool_uses (fibre-functor conservativity, finite and étale fpqc descent). No changes.
